pa_brown_rocks_main_wall.blurb: A quartzite wall on the northwest flank of Monalto Mountain in Franklin County, looking out over the Cumberland Valley. Fourteen climbs, nearly all of them traditionally protected single pitches that top out around 45 feet, with one boulder problem. The spread is wide, from easy chimneys and low fifth-class lines through the middle grades up to a few hard 5.11 leads, so there is something for most trad climbers. Because the pitches are short and finish at solid tops, it also works well as a top-rope venue. Expect a walk-in along the base of the ridge that crosses a large scree field before the wall appears.

pa_9_spire_and_facade.blurb: Two small features stacked close together inside Susquehanna Riverlands State Park on the west bank of the Susquehanna: a freestanding spire and a short wall beside it. Fourteen climbs, mostly trad and top rope, with three boulder problems. Grades sit at the friendly end, from around 5.2 up to a handful of 5.9 and 5.10 lines, so beginners and moderate leaders are well served. The quartzite is lightly traveled, so expect some loose rock and bring a helmet; lines clean up with use. It makes a quick add-on stop while visiting the neighboring Castellan and Gibraltar walls rather than a destination on its own.

pa_d_zorro_wall.blurb: A sport face in Birdsboro Quarry, a former quarry near Reading in the state's southeastern lowlands. All fourteen routes are bolted, and the grades are mostly in the moderate range: a few low-5.6 to 5.8 warm-ups, a solid cluster of 5.9 and 5.10 lines, then one or two 5.11s and a 5.12 near the top end. The quarry rock is diabase cut by machines, so loose pieces are more common than on a natural cliff and a helmet is wise. To find it, head left from the entrance sign past the Main Wall and the Orange Sunshine Wall; the face stands out on your left.

pa_k_the_wall_of_immortals.blurb: The big, imposing wall on the reservoir side of Birdsboro Quarry, a former quarry in southeastern Pennsylvania. Fourteen bolted sport routes, tilted toward the hard end: a lone 5.7 and a pair of 5.8s, a couple of 5.10s and 5.11s, and then a stack of 5.12s and 5.13s that make up most of the wall. It is a destination for strong sport climbers rather than beginners. The cut diabase here has shed a lot of loose rock, especially on the lower pitches, so wear a helmet and keep belayers alert. The base lies on the left side of the water, off the trail that runs closest to the reservoir.

pa_b_orange_sunshine_wall.blurb: A smaller wall inside Birdsboro Quarry, a former quarry in southeastern Pennsylvania, reached through a gap just past the long Main Wall on the path left from the entrance sign. Thirteen climbs: ten bolted sport routes and three mixed lines at about M6. The sport grades start in the 5.5 to 5.8 range, so there are easy options for newer leaders, and build through 5.9 and 5.10 to a pair of 5.11s. The namesake 5.8 is the most-traveled line. As on the rest of the quarry, the walls are machine cut and carry more loose rock than a natural crag, so a helmet is a good idea.

pa_3_0_euro_wall.blurb: A steep, thin-featured sport wall along the Susquehanna rail trail in the Safe Harbor North section, roughly 25 minutes southwest of Lancaster. It holds thirteen routes, twelve of them sport and one that doubles as a top rope. This is a hard-climber's wall: most lines are 5.12, with a few 5.10 and 5.11 routes and a single 5.8 and a 5.13 at either end. The rock stays dry and is usually sheltered from wind, and it catches sun through the winter, which makes it a good cold-weather pick. In summer it falls into shade before midday and again late afternoon. It is a fairly long walk or bike ride from the parking.

pa_middle_wall_2.blurb: A section of the Pike Run sandstone cliffs in Forbes State Forest, sitting just left of the Right Wall. Thirteen climbs, almost all top ropes anchored from bolts on a big boulder above the wall, plus one boulder problem. Grades run from about 5.5 up to 5.10, so it reaches a bit harder than the neighboring sections, with a large roof as the centerpiece and moves such as heel hooks. The short walls suit a relaxed day with a group. Reaching the anchors means a short scramble around the corner toward Tenderfoot Wall. A pad is worth carrying for the lines under the roof.
